claim_boundary: Exact algebraic audit conditional on the cited published zero-density estimates and the stated sufficient criteria in their short-interval proof. It is not an independent proof of those analytic estimates or of either short-interval theorem.

published_hypotheses_used: |sum_(n=N)^(2N) b_n n^(i*t_r)| >= V for every r

strict_gain.conclusion: T^(13/25+o(1)) versus T^(3/5+o(1)); gain 2/25 in the T exponent.

crossover.sign_conclusion: Ingham <= Guth--Maynard for sigma <= 7/10; Guth--Maynard <= Ingham for sigma >= 7/10.

frozen_hypotheses.almost_all_sufficient_criterion: As used in the cited proof: T=delta^(-1) times a subpower factor must satisfy T < X^(2/b-epsilon), and the reduction requires y >= delta*X.
frozen_hypotheses.counting_convention: N(sigma,T) counts zeros rho of zeta with Re(rho)>=sigma and |Im(rho)|<=T, with multiplicity.
frozen_hypotheses.uniform_short_interval_sufficient_criter: As used in the cited proof: with b the uniform density coefficient and T=x/y times a subpower factor, it is enough that T < x^(1/b-epsilon).

almost_all.classification: REPLAYED from the source's stated almost-all reduction; only its rational exponent conversion is independently checked here. This certificate does not independently derive the mean-square/explicit-formula argument.

uniform.classification: PROVED exact consequence of the stated sufficient criterion; the underlying explicit-formula criterion is a cited analytic input.
